recommendations: Mengshi Wang “I had the pleasure of working with Rohan as his manager, and I can confidently say he is a talented and driven young engineer with a genuine passion for technology. Rohan stands out for his excellent communication skills, ability to work highly independently, and strong ownership of projects from start to finish. During his time in our AI Studio, he took full ownership of refactoring our open-source Hybrid RAG project, elevating it from a research prototype to a production-grade system suitable for enterprise use. He went even further by packaging it as a clean, reusable tool that our AI agents could reliably call in real-world workflows. I recommend Rohan for any team looking for a capable, self-motivated AI/software engineer who combines strong technical ability with great communication and ownership. He would be a valuable asset to any forward-thinking organization.”

Belvedir (YC S26) is making private AI models cheap and easy, so the world can have trillions of them. In the past year, many big companies started paying millions of dollars to make internal private AI models. These models are cheaper, better, faster, and protect the company’s data from frontier labs. But right now these models are still only realistic for big companies since they’re really difficult and expensive to build. Belvedir makes private AI models autonomously with less than 5 minutes of setup, so that private AI can finally be accessible to startups and eventually everyone. Belvedir is live with 10 companies who are seeing up to 10x lower inference costs and 2x improved performance on benchmarks. Congrats on the launch, Zachary Yu ! 🚀 https://lnkd.in/gaG7KT7K

I'm incredibly grateful to share that I'll be joining Amazon this Fall as a Software Development Engineer Intern on the Agentic AI DevOps team in Vancouver. A special thanks to Lauren Elize Roque , Wing Fung Lau and Jason Wong for believing in what I could become, not just what I had already done. Here's to the next iteration ✨✨✨

Graduated from the The London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) with a First Class Honours, receiving a distinction in all of my final modules. 🎓 Three years ago, I arrived at LSE with a lot of excitement and a lot of impostor syndrome. Having ranked 3rd nationally in India’s board examinations, I thought I had proven to myself that I was capable. Yet walking into LSE, surrounded by incredibly talented people from around the world, I found myself questioning whether I truly belonged. I never imagined I’d be graduating with a First Class degree and distinctions across all of my final-year modules. So, to anyone who has ever felt like they don’t belong in the room they’re in: you do!!! Don’t let impostor syndrome convince you otherwise. LSE has shaped me in ways I could never have anticipated. Over the past four years, I’ve had the privilege of receiving the Laidlaw Foundation Scholarship, later returning to deliver a speech at the Laidlaw graduation ceremony; receiving a LSE Department of International Relations grant to undertake policy work; founding The Commonwealth Youth Nexus; and working across UK House of Lords , the Civil Service Fast Stream , international organisations and journalism while balancing around 20 hours of work each week alongside my degree. When I first arrived, I certainly didn’t think I would graduate having written 3 research papers, built initiatives I care deeply about, and met people who have challenged, supported and inspired me every step of the way. None of this would have been possible without the friends, mentors and faculty who believed in me, often before I believed in myself. I’m incredibly grateful for everything LSE has given me, and excited to see where the next chapter leads.
